messages:
alex: Heads-up — during a private deploy test I saw repeated KMS decrypt errors from the keystore sidecar in the onprem VPC. Not seeing failed pod restarts but audit logs show a lot of 403-like failures. anyone available to triage?
priya: can you paste the exact log lines and which tenant? we should know whether this is RBAC or KMS policy.
alex: tenant: atlas-dev, agent: keystore-sidecar-0, logs: ```2026-03-19T14:02:11Z ERR keystore decrypt failed: access denied (KMS::PolicyDenied) key_id=projects/prod/keys/priv-keystore ctx=pod/keystore-sidecar-0```
samir: @alex thanks. that error smells like either key policy or the service account token used by the sidecar. is this the new ephemeral creds flow?
alex: yes, ephemeral creds via the attestation service. token exchange looked fine earlier in the pipeline.
lena: quick checklist: 1) check KMS key IAM bindings 2) check synched key policy on HSM/KMS cluster 3) confirm pod's projected token audience matches the attestor 4) netpols allowing egress to KMS control plane
priya: also check audit pipeline — our central audit may be dropping or redacting the full error message. can you grep control-plane logs for corresponding authorize decisions?
alex: ran `kubectl logs keystore-sidecar-0 -n atlas-dev | grep -i decrypt` — only the single line above. no extra stacktrace.
priya: run the attestation debug: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://attest.internal/v1/validate` see if it returns principal with correct iam:roles/keystore-access binding.
samir: if attestor is OK, next suspect is KMS key rotation or threshold policy — we recently applied a rotation window that added a conditional binding for onprem-reg. if the conditional checks for sourceIP and our NAT changed -> policy denied.
lena: good call. check KMS -> Key details -> IAM conditions. Also confirm the control-plane egress IPs in the VPC haven't changed after the last NAT bounce.
alex: quick check: NAT range unchanged. KMS bindings show a conditional `request.network == projects/myproj/global/networks/onprem-vpc` — our requests are coming from proxied jumpbox host IPs so mismatch.
priya: that explains it. mitigation options: 1) expand condition to include jumpbox CIDR 2) proxy attestation and inject correct network tag 3) fallback to dedicated key for this env and rotate later.
samir: for immediate recovery I vote for temporary broadened condition + ticket to rotate with stricter rule after we migrate proxies. also add an audit entry that ties the temporal change to the incident id.
lena: I'll draft the runbook step: add CIDR -> validate decrypt -> revert in 48h with change window. also add a postmortem checklist: root cause, why network proxy IPs shifted, and tla; include required approvals for future condition changes.
alex: doing the temporary change now. posting the patch diff for infra review: ```gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding priv-keystore --member=serviceAccount:keystore@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter --condition="expr=request.network == 'projects/myproj/global/networks/onprem-vpc' || request.peer.ip in ['10.18.0.0/22']"```
infra-bot: Deploy job queued: infra/keystore-policy/patch-37 -> staging-run (ETA 2m) :gear:
deploy-bot: Verified on staging, smoke decrypt OK. promoting to prod after 15m cooldown.
priya: please also add an audit log link to the ticket and enable more verbose keystore logging for 1 hour during the rollback window to capture any other failures.
samir: noted — I'll add a short incident response blurb and map to CVE process (no vuln found, policy mismatch).
lena: thanks team. after prod change we'll schedule a tabletop to cover 'conditional IAM and network proxies' in the private deployments playbook. :thumbsup:
